outcome: No resolution, partial resolution, or bound on the stated conjecture was found since 26 January 2024; active adjacent structural work continues but does not settle whether categoricity in aleph_n for all n implies categoricity in every cardinal for atomic classes.
summary: This bullet asks whether an atomic class (the class of atomic models of a complete first-order theory, equivalently models of a complete sentence of L_{omega_1,omega}) that is categorical in aleph_n for every n < omega must be categorical in every cardinal. The classical background (pre-2024, hence not part of this window) is Shelah's theorem that under the weak continuum hypothesis below aleph_omega, a sentence of L_{omega_1,omega} categorical in aleph_n for every n is categorical in all uncountable cardinals for EXCELLENT atomic classes; excellence was the extra hypothesis needed, and whether it can be dropped (or derived) for general atomic classes was left open. Searching for developments since 26 January 2024, I found an active line of work by Baldwin, Laskowski and Shelah that is adjacent but does not resolve this question. 'When does aleph_1-categoricity imply omega-stability?' (arXiv:2308.13942, submitted 2023-08-26, published in Model Theory 3 (2024), 801-823) proves that an aleph_1-categorical atomic class with a model of size beth_1^+ (or, per one source's phrasing, (2^aleph_0)^+) is omega-stable -- a structural/stability result that is a step toward understanding the excellence-type hypotheses used in the older categoricity-transfer machinery, but it is a sufficient condition for omega-stability, not a resolution of the stated transfer conjecture, and its submission predates the window's start by five months in any case (it is itself open_stale territory as a pre-window event, though I am not using it as the decisive event since it does not settle the question). 'An analogue of U-rank for atomic classes' (arXiv:2502.00984, submitted 2025-02-03) develops an ordinal-valued rank for atomic classes and proves structural dichotomies (unranked types force 2^aleph_1 non-isomorphic models of size aleph_1; when all ranks are finite, the rank is additive and tuples are dominated by independent pseudo-minimal realizations). This is explicitly framed by the authors as part of a 20+ year program to either fill Shelah's gap or show no counterexample exists by proving aleph_1-categoricity implies omega-stability in general -- i.e. it is building toward the machinery that might eventually bear on categoricity transfer, but it neither proves nor disproves the aleph_n-for-all-n implies every-cardinal statement as such. No paper found addresses AI involvement of any kind; searches for funding/acknowledgement text on both papers surfaced only standard NSF/BSF/Simons grant lines, no mention of AI, machine learning, or automated theorem-proving. No withdrawal, no counterexample, and no claimed proof of the conjecture were found anywhere in the window. I therefore classify this as open with no_change_found true.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2023-08-26-submitted Baldwin-Laskowski-Shelah paper's 2024 journal publication constitutes an 'event' worth dating to the window under the journal-publication exception noted in the instructions (journal date normally excluded, but the paper's public preprint predates the window regardless, so by the first-written-argument rule (S6.3) it is correctly excluded). Also, a reader could see the U-rank paper as 'progress' on the broader categoricity-transfer program in a loose sense; I did not code it as progress because it does not move any bound or settle any case of the specific conjecture as stated (categorical in aleph_n for all n implies categorical in every cardinal) -- it is preparatory structural machinery for a related but distinct question (whether aleph_1-categoricity alone implies omega-stability), which is a case of a different, though closely related, conjecture in the same research program, not this bullet's conjecture.
what_would_settle_it: A paper proving (or refuting, via a categorical-in-all-aleph_n-but-not-everywhere example) the transfer statement for general (non-excellent) atomic classes, or a paper proving that categoricity in aleph_n for all n forces excellence (which combined with the older Shelah/WCH theorem would settle it under that hypothesis), would settle the question. Absent that, continued structural papers in the Baldwin-Laskowski-Shelah U-rank program are the place to watch.
